## Rule

**DECODED (Worker-2 2026-06-11).** ARC-GEN generator `task_8f2ea7aa` ("fractal2").
Input = a 9x9 grid holding ONE 3x3 sprite (single non-bg color c) placed in one of
the 9 3x3 blocks. Output = the 9x9 fractal: for each ON cell (R,C) of the 3x3
sprite, stamp the whole 3x3 sprite into output block (R,C). i.e.
`out_mask[3R+r, 3C+c] = sprite[R,C] AND sprite[r,c]` (= kron of the 3x3 sprite mask
with itself), recolored to c; everything else is bg 0. Single color throughout.

**Grid is ALWAYS 9x9** — generator `size=3` is a default with no override path
(`arc_gen.py` calls `generator()` with no args); grid = `size*size` = 9x9. Crop-to-9x9
is provably hidden-safe and every 9x9 cell is active (no in-crop padding), which
makes `foreground = 1 - ch0` exact (the 1-ch0 trap needs padding cells).

mod-3 sprite-collapse and v9's free-output 2-term Einsum, now F16.
- **ONE dilated Conv does channel-collapse AND mod-3 block-OR**: `nbsum = Conv(input,
  wconv[1,10,3,3], dilations=[3,3], pads=[0,0,-21,-21])` -> `[1,1,3,3]` F32 36 B. `wconv` = ones
  with ch0 zeroed (collapse presence ch1..9); the dilation-3 taps over the 9x9 sum the 3
  block-rows/cols == the mod-3 block-OR. Single sprite => sum is already 0/1, no threshold.
  This ELIMINATES every 9x9 intermediate (v9's `ch0_crop` [1,1,9,9] F32 alone was 324 B, the
  single biggest charge in v9, plus the whole ArgMax/Gather/Where sprite-locate path).

  output. `t0` term = `kron(mask,mask)*fg-color` via `sel-2*e0`; `t1` term = all-ones tile *
  `e0` stamps ch0 across the 9x9 so bg cells decode to color 0; cells >=9 stay all-zero.
  Bases `Pb/Pt[30,3]` stay 30-axis (params; cropping to [9,3] forces a 30x30 re-pad = net loss).
- Largest charged intermediate = **40 B** (`sel4 [1,10,1,1] F32` / `sel2 [1,2,10] F16`).
  memory 230, params 304 (Pb 90 + Pt 90 + wconv 90 + e0 10 + two_e0 10 + ones13 9 + axes 5).

## Algorithm sketch

33 nodes, opset 10. Key:
1. 3× `Cast(input, F16)` → input_cast_to_44/66/69 [1,10,30,30] F16 = 18000B each (2 duplicates eliminated in v1)
2. `ch_nonbg = Gather(input_cast_to_44, [1..9], axis=1)` → [1,9,30,30] = 16200B
3. `nonbg = ReduceMax(ch_nonbg, axis=1)` → [1,1,30,30]; `nonbg_rs = Reshape → [1,30,30]`
4. `ArgMax + Gather chains` for pattern detection
5. `Where(cond, color_out, bg_out)` → final output

## Don't-do log

- 2026-05-18 | fp16_selective: +26288 cost increase (regression from spread scan). Do not apply.
- 2026-06-21 [w6] | DepthToSpace(CRD) outer-min canvas (#80) builds the 9x9 fractal cheaply
  (`canvas [1,1,9,9] U8`, chain ~570 B) BUT its 30x30 OUTPUT tail re-introduces a big charged
  intermediate: Equal-tail `Pad(canvas)->[1,1,30,30] U8` = 900 B (tail A, cost 1617) or
  small-onehot `Equal(canvas)->[1,10,9,9] BOOL` = 810 B (tail B, cost 1527). Both LOSE to v9's
  einsum because the einsum emits the 30x30 free output with NO 30x30/810 intermediate. The
  D2S `canvas` builder is staged-quality only as a single-channel artifact (708 at 9x9 I/O, but
  9x9 I/O is invalid — the real input is always [1,10,30,30]). Lesson: for a fully-generated
  30x30 colored output, the free-output Einsum beats D2S+Pad/Equal every time; D2S wins only
  when the canvas itself can BE the (small) output. Dead-end ONNX:
  `task217/prototypes/task217_d2s_{A,B}.onnx`.
- 2026-06-21 [w6] | Cropping v9's M_block/M_tile bases from [30,3] to [9,3] shrinks the einsum
  output to [1,10,9,9]; re-padding to 30x30 then charges a ~3.2 KB intermediate (net loss).
  Keep the 30-axis bases as PARAMS (element-count, dtype-free) and emit 30x30 directly.
- 2026-06-21 [w6] | Cast(input,F16) before the channel-collapse Conv materializes the full
  [1,10,9,9] F16 = 1620 B (cost jumps to 2166). Conv reads F32 input directly (single-channel
  F32 out) is cheaper. Likewise reshape-first spatial collapse `[1,10,3,3,3,3]` keeps F32 at
  full 3240 B (cost 3850). Collapse CHANNELS first (Conv), never spatial-first.
- 2026-06-24 [w4] | FREE-INPUT mask3 Einsum (the p29 prompt's main hope) LOSES = 572 (>534).
  `mask3 = Einsum('bhIJ,h,Ir,Js->brs', input, collapse, Pt, Pt)` reads the F32 one-hot input
  directly (input operand free) and is numerically correct (4/4, reusing Pt for the mod-3
  collapse — Pt[I,t]=1 iff I%3==t IS the block-OR basis). BUT Einsum requires consistent operand
  dtype and `input` is F32, so the whole graph must run F32: either a duplicate F32 Pt (+90
  params, kills the saving) or an all-F32 graph that doubles every small intermediate
  (sel2/stack2/sel_flat) to F32 -> memory 230->344, cost 572. The dilated Conv's wconv[1,10,3,3]
  (90 params, F32-clean, single-channel F32 out 36 B) is already the optimal channel-collapse
  op; the free-input einsum cannot beat it because it needs a 2nd F32 placement basis. Dead-end
  ONNX: `task217/prototypes/task217_d2s_freeinput.onnx`. Lesson: a free-INPUT einsum only wins
  when its bases are NOT also needed in F16 downstream; here Pt is shared with the F16 kron einsum,
  so the dtype split forces a param/memory loss either way.
- 2026-06-24 [w4] | 532 is the free-output-kron FAMILY FLOOR. params = Pb(90)+Pt(90)+wconv(90)
  +e0(10)+two_e0(10)+ones13(9)+sel_shape(3) = 302; memory 230. The two [30,3] placement bases +
  [1,10,3,3] collapse conv (270) are structurally irreducible (block + tile placement of a
  3x3-kron-3x3 into a 30x30 free output). Selector consts floor at 20 (e0+two_e0 for the 2-row
  fg-color + bg-cancel selector). Only sub-534 lever was the opset-13 axes-as-attribute -2.
